ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there are 6 square regions in total. The upper row has three small squares, denoted from left to right as A, B, C; the right vertical column has two more small squares below C, denoted respectively as D, E; the lower left is a relatively larger square region, denoted as F. According to the situation of shared sides in the figure, the adjacent position pairs are AB, AF, BF, BC, CD, DF, DE, EF. Those that touch only at a corner do not count as adjacent; for example, C and F touch only at one corner point, so they are not adjacent. Reasoning: The problem requires that the difference between the numbers in adjacent squares cannot equal 3. Among the numbers 1,2,3,4,5,6, the unordered number pairs with difference 3 are only {1,4}, {2,5}, {3,6}. Therefore, the two numbers in these three number pairs must respectively be placed in a pair of non-adjacent positions. In other words, the 6 positions must be divided into 3 pairs of non-adjacent positions. Among the non-adjacent position pairs obtained from the adjacency relation, there are only two perfect matchings that can cover A,B,C,D,E,F: {AD, BE, CF} and {AE, BD, CF}. For each kind of position pairing, the three forbidden number pairs {1,4}, {2,5}, {3,6} can be assigned to these three pairs of positions, for a total of 3! ways; the two numbers inside each number pair can also be swapped, for a total of 2^3 ways. Therefore the total number is 2 · 3! · 2^3 = 96 = 3 · 2^5.

method.method_draft: First read the figure as six square regions: A = top-left small square, B = top-middle small square, C = top-right small square, D = middle-right small square, E = bottom-right small square, and F = the large lower-left square. From shared sides, the adjacent position pairs are AB, AF, BF, BC, CD, DF, DE, EF; pairs meeting only at a point, such as C and F, are not adjacent. From the text, the only forbidden numerical pairs are (1,4), (2,5), and (3,6), since these differ by 3. Therefore each forbidden numerical pair must occupy a nonadjacent pair of positions. Build the nonadjacency graph on A,B,C,D,E,F and find its perfect matchings. The only two perfect matchings by nonadjacent position-pairs are {AD, BE, CF} and {AE, BD, CF}. Assign the three numerical forbidden pairs to the three position-pairs in 3! ways, then orient the two numbers within each pair in 2^3 ways. This gives 2 · 3! · 2^3 = 96 = 3 · 2^5.
